<path>/workspace/ctx.go</path>
<type>file</type>
<content>
1: // ⚡️ Fiber is an Express inspired web framework written in Go with ☕️
2: // 🤖 GitHub Repository: https://github.com/gofiber/fiber
3: // 📌 API Documentation: https://docs.gofiber.io
4: 
5: package fiber
6: 
7: import (
8: 	"bytes"
9: 	"context"
10: 	"crypto/tls"
11: 	"fmt"
12: 	"io"
13: 	"maps"
14: 	"mime/multipart"
15: 	"strings"
16: 	"sync"
17: 	"sync/atomic"
18: 	"time"
19: 
20: 	"github.com/gofiber/utils/v2"
21: 	"github.com/valyala/bytebufferpool"
22: 	"github.com/valyala/fasthttp"
23: )
24: 
25: const (
26: 	schemeHTTP  = "http"
27: 	schemeHTTPS = "https"
28: )
29: 
30: const (
31: 	// maxParams defines the maximum number of parameters per route.
32: 	maxParams         = 30
33: 	maxDetectionPaths = 3
34: )
35: 
36: var (
37: 	_                  io.Writer       = (*DefaultCtx)(nil) // Compile-time check
38: 	_                  context.Context = (*DefaultCtx)(nil) // Compile-time check
39: 	emptyRouteHandlers [0]Handler
40: 	emptyRouteParams   [0]string
41: )
42: 
43: // The contextKey type is unexported to prevent collisions with context keys defined in
44: // other packages.
45: type contextKey int
46: 
47: // userContextKey define the key name for storing context.Context in *fasthttp.RequestCtx
48: const (
49: 	userContextKey contextKey = iota // __local_user_context__
50: )
51: 
52: // DefaultCtx is the default implementation of the Ctx interface
53: // generation tool `go install github.com/vburenin/ifacemaker@f30b6f9bdbed4b5c4804ec9ba4a04a999525c202`
54: // https://github.com/vburenin/ifacemaker/blob/f30b6f9bdbed4b5c4804ec9ba4a04a999525c202/ifacemaker.go#L14-L31
55: //
56: //go:generate ifacemaker --file ctx.go --file req.go --file res.go --struct DefaultCtx --iface Ctx --pkg fiber --promoted --output ctx_interface_gen.go --not-exported true --iface-comment "Ctx represents the Context which hold the HTTP request and response.\nIt has methods for the request query string, parameters, body, HTTP headers and so on."
57: type DefaultCtx struct {
58: 	handlerCtx             CustomCtx            // Active custom context implementation, if any
59: 	DefaultReq                                  // Default request api
60: 	DefaultRes                                  // Default response api
61: 	app                    *App                 // Reference to *App
62: 	route                  *Route               // Reference to *Route
63: 	fasthttp               *fasthttp.RequestCtx // Reference to *fasthttp.RequestCtx
64: 	bind                   *Bind                // Default bind reference
65: 	redirect               *Redirect            // Default redirect reference
66: 	reclaim                *reclaimLatch        // Coordinates safe pool reclamation of an abandoned ctx; nil on the hot path
67: 	viewBindMap            Map                  // Default view map to bind template engine
68: 	values                 [maxParams]string    // Route parameter values
69: 	baseURI                string               // HTTP base uri
70: 	pathOriginal           string               // Original HTTP path
71: 	flashMessages          redirectionMsgs      // Flash messages
72: 	path                   []byte               // HTTP path with the modifications by the configuration
73: 	detectionPath          []byte               // Route detection path
74: 	treePathHash           int                  // Hash of the path for the search in the tree
75: 	pathSlashes            int                  // Number of '/' in the detection path, used to quick-reject routes
76: 	indexRoute             int                  // Index of the current route
77: 	indexHandler           int                  // Index of the current handler
78: 	firstMatchIndex        int                  // Pre-resolved endpoint index from the SkipUnmatchedRoutes lookahead; -1 when unused
79: 	methodInt              int                  // HTTP method INT equivalent
80: 	isAbandoned            atomic.Bool          // If true, ctx won't be pooled until ForceRelease is called
81: 	isMatched              bool                 // Non use route matched
82: 	shouldSkipNonUseRoutes bool                 // Skip non-use routes while iterating middleware
83: 	isUserContextSet       bool                 // User context was stored in fasthttp user values
84: }
85: 
86: // TLSHandler hosts the callback hooks Fiber invokes while negotiating TLS
87: // connections, including optional client certificate lookups.
88: type TLSHandler struct {
89: 	clientHelloInfo *tls.ClientHelloInfo
90: }
91: 
92: // GetClientInfo Callback function to set ClientHelloInfo
93: // Must comply with the method structure of https://cs.opensource.google/go/go/+/refs/tags/go1.20:src/crypto/tls/common.go;l=554-563
94: // Since we overlay the method of the TLS config in the listener method
95: func (t *TLSHandler) GetClientInfo(info *tls.ClientHelloInfo) (*tls.Certificate, error) {
96: 	t.clientHelloInfo = info
97: 	return nil, nil //nolint:nilnil // Not returning anything useful here is probably fine
98: }
99: 
100: // Views is the interface that wraps the Render function.
101: type Views interface {
102: 	Load() error
103: 	Render(out io.Writer, name string, binding any, layout ...string) error
104: }
105: 
106: // App returns the *App reference to the instance of the Fiber application
107: func (c *DefaultCtx) App() *App {
108: 	return c.app
109: }
110: 
111: // BaseURL returns (protocol + host + base path).
112: func (c *DefaultCtx) BaseURL() string {
113: 	// TODO: Could be improved: 53.8 ns/op  32 B/op  1 allocs/op
114: 	// Should work like https://codeigniter.com/user_guide/helpers/url_helper.html
115: 	if c.baseURI != "" {
116: 		return c.baseURI
117: 	}
118: 	scheme := c.Scheme()
119: 	host := c.Host()
120: 	buf := make([]byte, 0, len(scheme)+len("://")+len(host))
121: 	buf = append(buf, scheme...)
122: 	buf = append(buf, "://"...)
123: 	buf = append(buf, host...)
124: 	c.baseURI = c.app.toString(buf)
125: 	return c.baseURI
126: }
127:

249: // Next executes the next method in the stack that matches the current route.
250: func (c *DefaultCtx) Next() error {
251: 	// Increment handler index
252: 	c.indexHandler++
253: 
254: 	// Did we execute all route handlers?
255: 	if c.indexHandler < len(c.route.Handlers) {
256: 		if c.handlerCtx != nil {
257: 			return c.route.Handlers[c.indexHandler](c.handlerCtx)
258: 		}
259: 		return c.route.Handlers[c.indexHandler](c)
260: 	}
261: 
262: 	if c.handlerCtx != nil {
263: 		_, err := c.app.nextCustom(c.handlerCtx)
264: 		return err
265: 	}
266: 	_, err := c.app.next(c)
267: 	return err
268: }

278: 		return err
279: 	}
280: 	_, err := c.app.next(c)
281: 	return err

374: // routeFallback builds the synthetic route for the fasthttp error handler.

376: // fallback for unregistered methods) so Route and Method always agree.

412: // HasBody returns true if the request declares a body via Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding, or already buffered payload data.
413: func (c *DefaultCtx) HasBody() bool {
414: 	hdr := &c.fasthttp.Request.Header
415: 
416: 	switch cl := hdr.ContentLength(); {
417: 	case cl > 0:
418: 		return true
419: 	case cl == -1:
420: 		// fasthttp reports -1 for Transfer-Encoding: chunked bodies.
421: 		return true
422: 	case cl == 0:
423: 		if hasTransferEncodingBody(hdr) {
424: 			return true
425: 		}
426: 	}
427: 
428: 	return len(c.fasthttp.Request.Body()) > 0
429: }

431: // OverrideParam overwrites a route parameter value by name.
432: // If the parameter name does not exist in the route, this method does nothing.
433: func (c *DefaultCtx) OverrideParam(name, value string) {
434: 	// If no route is matched, there are no parameters to update
435: 	if !c.Matched() {
436: 		return
437: 	}
438: 
439: 	// Normalize wildcard (*) and plus (+) tokens to their internal
440: 	// representations (*1, +1) used by the router.
441: 	if name == "*" || name == "+" {
442: 		name += "1"
443: 	}
444: 
445: 	if c.app.config.CaseSensitive {
446: 		for i, param := range c.route.Params {
447: 			if param == name {
448: 				c.values[i] = value
449: 				return
450: 			}
451: 		}
452: 		return
453: 	}
454: 
455: 	nameBytes := utils.UnsafeBytes(name)
456: 	for i, param := range c.route.Params {
457: 		if utils.EqualFold(utils.UnsafeBytes(param), nameBytes) {
458: 			c.values[i] = value
459: 			return
460: 		}
461: 	}
462: }

464: func hasTransferEncodingBody(hdr *fasthttp.RequestHeader) bool {
465: 	// Repeated field lines form one combined list (RFC 9110 Section 5.2),
466: 	// so every Transfer-Encoding line must be inspected, not just the first.
467: 	if lines := hdr.PeekAll(HeaderTransferEncoding); len(lines) > 0 {
468: 		for _, line := range lines {
469: 			if transferEncodingLineHasBody(utils.UnsafeString(line)) {
470: 				return true
471: 			}
472: 		}
473: 		return false
474: 	}
475: 
476: 	// Fallback scan for non-normalized header keys.
477: 	for key, value := range hdr.All() {
478: 		if !utils.EqualFold(utils.UnsafeString(key), HeaderTransferEncoding) {
479: 			continue
480: 		}
481: 		if transferEncodingLineHasBody(utils.UnsafeString(value)) {
482: 			return true
483: 		}
484: 	}
485: 
486: 	return false
487: }
488: 
489: // transferEncodingLineHasBody reports whether a single Transfer-Encoding
490: // field line contains a transfer coding other than "identity".
491: func transferEncodingLineHasBody(te string) bool {
492: 	for raw := range strings.SplitSeq(te, ",") {
493: 		token := utils.TrimSpace(raw)
494: 		if token == "" {
495: 			continue
496: 		}
497: 		if idx := strings.IndexByte(token, ';'); idx >= 0 {
498: 			token = utils.TrimSpace(token[:idx])
499: 		}
500: 		if token == "" {
501: 			continue
502: 		}
503: 		if utils.EqualFold(token, "identity") {
504: 			continue
505: 		}
506: 		return true
507: 	}
508: 	return false
509: }

511: // IsWebSocket returns true if the request includes a WebSocket upgrade handshake.
512: func (c *DefaultCtx) IsWebSocket() bool {
513: 	// Repeated field lines are equivalent to one combined comma-separated
514: 	// list (RFC 9110 Section 5.2), so inspect every Connection and Upgrade
515: 	// field line, not just the first.
516: 	if !headerListContainsToken(c.fasthttp.Request.Header.PeekAll(HeaderConnection), "upgrade") {
517: 		return false
518: 	}
519: 	// Upgrade is a list of protocols, each optionally carrying a "/version"
520: 	// suffix (RFC 9110 Section 7.8), e.g. "Upgrade: websocket, h2c".
521: 	return headerListContainsToken(c.fasthttp.Request.Header.PeekAll(HeaderUpgrade), "websocket")
522: }
523: 
524: // headerListContainsToken reports whether any comma-separated element across
525: // the given field lines equals token case-insensitively. An optional
526: // "/version" suffix (Upgrade protocol syntax, RFC 9110 Section 7.8) is
527: // ignored when comparing; valid Connection members never contain "/", so
528: // this is safe for both headers.
529: func headerListContainsToken(lines [][]byte, token string) bool {
530: 	for _, line := range lines {
531: 		for v := range strings.SplitSeq(utils.UnsafeString(line), ",") {
532: 			element := utils.TrimSpace(v)
533: 			if i := strings.IndexByte(element, '/'); i >= 0 {
534: 				element = element[:i]
535: 			}
536: 			if utils.EqualFold(element, token) {
537: 				return true
538: 			}
539: 		}
540: 	}
541: 	return false
542: }

564: // SaveFileToStorage saves any multipart file to an external storage system.
565: func (c *DefaultCtx) SaveFileToStorage(fileheader *multipart.FileHeader, path string, storage Storage) error {
566: 	if fileheader == nil {
567: 		return ErrFileHeaderNil
568: 	}
569: 
570: 	file, err := fileheader.Open()
571: 	if err != nil {
572: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %q: %w", ErrFileOpen, fileheader.Filename, err)
573: 	}
574: 	defer file.Close() //nolint:errcheck // not needed
575: 
576: 	maxUploadSize := c.app.config.BodyLimit
577: 	if maxUploadSize <= 0 {
578: 		maxUploadSize = DefaultBodyLimit
579: 	}
580: 
581: 	if fileheader.Size > 0 && fileheader.Size > int64(maxUploadSize) {
582: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %q: %w", ErrFileRead, fileheader.Filename, fasthttp.ErrBodyTooLarge)
583: 	}
584: 
585: 	buf := bytebufferpool.Get()
586: 	defer bytebufferpool.Put(buf)
587: 
588: 	limitedReader := io.LimitReader(file, int64(maxUploadSize)+1)
589: 	if _, err = buf.ReadFrom(limitedReader); err != nil {
590: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %q: %w", ErrFileRead, fileheader.Filename, err)
591: 	}
592: 
593: 	if buf.Len() > maxUploadSize {
594: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %q: %w", ErrFileRead, fileheader.Filename, fasthttp.ErrBodyTooLarge)
595: 	}
596: 
597: 	data := append([]byte(nil), buf.Bytes()...)
598: 
599: 	if err := storage.SetWithContext(c.Context(), path, data, 0); err != nil {
600: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %q to %q: %w", ErrFileStore, fileheader.Filename, path, err)
601: 	}
602: 
603: 	return nil
604: }

618: // String returns unique string representation of the ctx.
619: //
620: // The returned value may be useful for logging.
621: func (c *DefaultCtx) String() string {
622: 	// Get buffer from pool
623: 	buf := bytebufferpool.Get()
624: 
625: 	// Start with the ID, converting it to a hex string without fmt.Sprintf
626: 	buf.WriteByte('#')
627: 	const hex = "0123456789abcdef"
628: 	var id [16]byte
629: 	ctxID := c.fasthttp.ID()
630: 	for i := len(id) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
631: 		id[i] = hex[ctxID&0xf]
632: 		ctxID >>= 4
633: 	}
634: 	buf.Write(id[:])
635: 	buf.WriteString(" - ")
636: 
637: 	// Add local and remote addresses directly
638: 	buf.WriteString(c.fasthttp.LocalAddr().String())
639: 	buf.WriteString(" <-> ")
640: 	buf.WriteString(c.fasthttp.RemoteAddr().String())
641: 	buf.WriteString(" - ")
642: 
643: 	// Add method and URI
644: 	buf.Write(c.fasthttp.Request.Header.Method())
645: 	buf.WriteByte(' ')
646: 	buf.Write(c.fasthttp.URI().FullURI())
647: 
648: 	// Allocate string
649: 	str := buf.String()
650: 
651: 	// Reset buffer
652: 	buf.Reset()
653: 	bytebufferpool.Put(buf)
654: 
655: 	return str
656: }

677: // configDependentPaths set paths for route recognition and prepared paths for the user,
678: // here the features for caseSensitive, decoded paths, strict paths are evaluated
679: func (c *DefaultCtx) configDependentPaths() {
680: 	c.path = append(c.path[:0], c.pathOriginal...)
681: 	// If UnescapePath enabled, we decode the path and save it for the framework user
682: 	if c.app.config.UnescapePath {
683: 		c.path = fasthttp.AppendUnquotedArg(c.path[:0], c.path)
684: 	}
685: 
686: 	// another path is specified which is for routing recognition only
687: 	// use the path that was changed by the previous configuration flags
688: 	// If CaseSensitive is disabled, we lowercase the original path while
689: 	// copying it, fusing the copy and the case fold into a single pass.
690: 	if !c.app.config.CaseSensitive {
691: 		c.detectionPath = appendLowerASCII(c.detectionPath[:0], c.path)
692: 	} else {
693: 		c.detectionPath = append(c.detectionPath[:0], c.path...)
694: 	}
695: 	// If StrictRouting is disabled, we strip all trailing slashes
696: 	if !c.app.config.StrictRouting && len(c.detectionPath) > 1 && c.detectionPath[len(c.detectionPath)-1] == '/' {
697: 		c.detectionPath = utils.TrimRight(c.detectionPath, '/')
698: 	}
699: 
700: 	// Define the path for dividing routes into areas for fast tree detection, so that fewer routes need to be traversed,
701: 	// since the first three characters area select a list of routes
702: 	c.treePathHash = 0
703: 	if len(c.detectionPath) >= maxDetectionPaths {
704: 		c.treePathHash = int(c.detectionPath[0])<<16 |
705: 			int(c.detectionPath[1])<<8 |
706: 			int(c.detectionPath[2])
707: 	}
708: 
709: 	// Invalidate the cached slash count of the detection path; pathSlashCount
710: 	// recomputes it lazily when route matching first needs it.
711: 	c.pathSlashes = 0
712: }

714: // Reset is a method to reset context fields by given request when to use server handlers.
715: func (c *DefaultCtx) Reset(fctx *fasthttp.RequestCtx) {
716: 	// Reset route and handler index
717: 	c.indexRoute = -1
718: 	c.indexHandler = 0
719: 	// Reset matched flag
720: 	c.isMatched = false
721: 	c.shouldSkipNonUseRoutes = false
722: 	c.firstMatchIndex = -1
723: 	// Set paths
724: 	c.pathOriginal = c.app.toString(fctx.URI().PathOriginal())
725: 	// Set method
726: 	c.methodInt = c.app.methodInt(utils.UnsafeString(fctx.Request.Header.Method()))
727: 	// Attach *fasthttp.RequestCtx to ctx
728: 	c.fasthttp = fctx
729: 	// reset base uri
730: 	c.baseURI = ""
731: 	// Prettify path
732: 	c.configDependentPaths()
733: 
734: 	c.DefaultReq.c = c
735: 	c.DefaultRes.c = c
736: }

738: // release is a method to reset context fields when to use ReleaseCtx()
739: func (c *DefaultCtx) release() {
740: 	if c.isUserContextSet {
741: 		if c.fasthttp != nil {
742: 			c.fasthttp.SetUserValue(userContextKey, nil)
743: 		}
744: 		c.isUserContextSet = false
745: 	}
746: 	c.route = nil

749: 		ReleaseBind(c.bind)
750: 		c.bind = nil
751: 	}
752: 	c.flashMessages = c.flashMessages[:0]
753: 	// Clear viewBindMap by deleting all keys (reuse underlying map if possible)
754: 	if c.viewBindMap != nil {
755: 		clear(c.viewBindMap)
756: 	}
757: 	if c.redirect != nil {
758: 		ReleaseRedirect(c.redirect)
759: 		c.redirect = nil
760: 	}
761: 	c.shouldSkipNonUseRoutes = false
762: 	// performance: no need for using c.isAbandoned.Store(false) here, as it is always set to false when it was true in ForceRelease
763: 	c.reclaim = nil
764: 	c.handlerCtx = nil
765: }
766: 
767: // reclaimLatch coordinates the safe, automatic reclamation of an abandoned
768: // context back into the pool. It is armed only via ScheduleReclaim (currently by
769: // the timeout middleware) and stays nil on the common request path, so requests
770: // that are not abandoned pay no additional cost.
771: type reclaimLatch struct {
772: 	releasedCh chan struct{} // closed once the request handler has released the ctx (event b)
773: 	once       sync.Once     // guards the close-exactly-once of releasedCh
774: }
775: 
776: // Abandon marks this context as abandoned. An abandoned context will not be
777: // returned to the pool when ReleaseCtx is called.
778: //
779: // This is used by the timeout and SSE middlewares to return immediately while a
780: // goroutine continues using the context safely.
781: //
782: // Only call ForceRelease after Abandon if you can guarantee no other goroutine
783: // (including Fiber's requestHandler and ErrorHandler) will touch the context.
784: // Callers that cannot make that guarantee themselves can instead call
785: // ScheduleReclaim, which arranges a race-free ForceRelease once the handler has
786: // finished and the request handler has released the context.
787: func (c *DefaultCtx) Abandon() {
788: 	c.isAbandoned.Store(true)
789: }
790: 
791: // IsAbandoned returns true if Abandon() was called on this context.
792: func (c *DefaultCtx) IsAbandoned() bool {
793: 	return c.isAbandoned.Load()
794: }
795: 
796: // ForceRelease releases an abandoned context back to the pool.
797: // This MUST only be called after all goroutines (including requestHandler and
798: // ErrorHandler) have completely finished using this context. Calling it while
799: // any goroutine is still running causes races.
800: func (c *DefaultCtx) ForceRelease() {
801: 	c.isAbandoned.Store(false)
802: 	c.app.ReleaseCtx(c)
803: }
804: 
805: // ScheduleReclaim arms automatic reclamation of an abandoned context, returning
806: // it to the pool once it is safe to do so.
807: //
808: // handlerDone must be closed once the goroutine that still uses this context
809: // (for the timeout middleware, the handler goroutine) has completely finished.
810: // cancel, if non-nil, is the CancelFunc of the context installed for that
811: // goroutine and is invoked as soon as it finishes.
812: //
813: // ForceRelease is performed only after BOTH handlerDone is closed AND the request
814: // handler has released the context (signaled from ReleaseCtx/releaseDefaultCtx),
815: // which makes the reclamation race-free. If handlerDone never closes — a handler
816: // that never returns — the context is intentionally never reclaimed, because the
817: // handler still owns it.
818: //
819: // This method calls Abandon internally, so callers do not need to call Abandon
820: // separately. Calling Abandon before ScheduleReclaim is still safe (idempotent).
821: func (c *DefaultCtx) ScheduleReclaim(handlerDone <-chan struct{}, cancel context.CancelFunc) {
822: 	c.Abandon()
823: 
824: 	latch := &reclaimLatch{releasedCh: make(chan struct{})}
825: 	c.reclaim = latch
826: 
827: 	go func() {
828: 		<-handlerDone
829: 		if cancel != nil {
830: 			cancel()
831: 		}
832: 		<-latch.releasedCh
833: 		c.ForceRelease()
834: 	}()
835: }

837: // signalReleased records that the request handler is done touching an abandoned,
838: // reclaim-armed context (event b). It is a no-op when reclamation was not armed
839: // and is safe to call multiple times.
840: func (c *DefaultCtx) signalReleased() {
841: 	if c.reclaim != nil {
842: 		c.reclaim.once.Do(func() {
843: 			close(c.reclaim.releasedCh)
844: 		})
845: 	}
846: }

848: func (c *DefaultCtx) renderExtensions(bind any) {
849: 	if bindMap, ok := bind.(Map); ok {
850: 		// Bind view map
851: 		for key, value := range c.viewBindMap {
852: 			if _, ok := bindMap[key]; !ok {

857: 		// Check if the PassLocalsToViews option is enabled (by default it is disabled)

864: 					bindMap[c.app.toString(key)] = val

866: 			})
867: 		}
868: 	}

870: 	c.app.mountFields.appListKeysOnce.Do(c.app.generateAppListKeys)
